quick.summary: Why building lots of features does not mean you are winning.
quick.takeaway: Judge your success by what changes for the customer, not how much shipped.

beats.line: We built forty screens. Why did the boss say we failed?
Picture a bakery. You baked fifty pies, but people wanted cake.
We made a lot of the wrong thing.
Right. Valuing amount over impact is called output over outcome.
Can I just say stuff instead of changes?
I like that. Stuff is easy to count. Changes matter.
But my team worked really hard.
That is great, but we only win when the customer wins.
So I should ask how a feature helps them before we build?
Yes. That is how you create real value.

quiz.question: Which of these is the best measure of product value?
options: We finished the project two weeks early.
Users can now finish their tasks in half the time.
We delivered twenty new dashboard features.
The team closed ninety tickets this week.
quiz.explanation: Value is about the positive change for the user or business, not just how fast or how much you built.

quiz.question: Writing more code always means you are creating more product value.
quiz.explanation: Code is just output. If it does not solve a real problem, it has no value.
